## ACCEPT — open question ruled **A: keep the implementation in `@object-ui/core`, re-exported from `@object-ui/fields`**

Reviewed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (session `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK`). No re-litigation of the maintainer's ruling — this is the only physically constructible reading of it.

### The ruling, verified independently

I re-derived the blocking fact on `origin/main` rather than taking it from the report:

- `packages/fields/package.json` → `dependencies` includes **`"@object-ui/components": "workspace:*"`**, and **54** files under `packages/fields/src/**` import from it. Your figure to the digit.
- `packages/core/package.json` → depends only on `@object-ui/types` (plus the two `@objectstack/*` externals).

So `@object-ui/components` is one of the six ruled consumers, and `fields` → `components` means **a table homed in `fields` cannot be imported by `components`**. The ruling's literal wording is not merely awkward here; it is unbuildable. Homing in `core` is the only placement that reaches all six without inverting an existing edge, and `core` already owns the sibling cross-package field-type vocabulary (`EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`), so the table lands next to its own family rather than in a new home invented for it.

**What the ruling actually asked for is preserved in full**, which is why A is a reading and not an exception:

| the ruling's clause | under A |
|---|---|
| "a single `isRetiredFieldType(t)` gate" | one function object — you deleted #4942's local copy in `FieldEditWidget.tsx` so it is literally the same function, not a matching one |
| "exported from `@object-ui/fields`" | `import { isRetiredFieldType } from '@object-ui/fields'` resolves — pinned by a test **and** proved through the checker against the built `.d.ts` |
| "fires **once**" | one `reportedRetiredTypes` set, cross-package, pinned |

**B fails the ruling's own third clause on day one** — two tables means two dedupe sets, so one spelling logs twice — and you did not argue that, you *measured* it: ablation leg 7 removes the dedupe and shows exactly what it looks like, 8 failures across all six files including the cross-package "the toolbar face and the filter-builder face share the dedupe set". **C** abandons the face the premise-gate measurement proved most live, where `operatorsForFieldType('owner')` matched the `user` bucket item for item and the 16th face is a positive pin on that exact conjunct.

Flagging it as an open question rather than burying it in the summary was right. A re-homing the reviewer discovers in the diff is a different thing from one the reviewer confirms.

### The best catch in this PR

> `deriveHighlightFields` also selects by **NAME** through a `preferred` list whose FIRST entry is `owner`, so gating only the type-driven loop would have left the exact shape this card is about — a field named `owner` still typed `owner` — reaching the strip through the other door **with the fix reading as complete**

The card names one door. You found two, and the second one is selected by the very spelling being retired. A fix that gates the door the card names and leaves the other open is worse than no fix, because the next reader sees a gated predicate and stops looking. Ablation leg 2 confirms both doors go red, and the surviving idiom `{ type: 'user', name: 'owner' }` keeps its slot, pinned — so the gate refuses the retired *type* without refusing a legitimate *name*.

### Two disposition calls that go beyond "add the gate"

**`retypeFilterValue` deliberately not gated** — because a refusal that cleared the row would *destroy a stored value on the way to showing the author the prescription*. The point of a loud refusal is to tell someone something; doing it in a way that eats their data first inverts the purpose.

**The refusal answers as an unrecognised spelling, not an empty bucket** — an empty operator bucket draws a blank trigger (#4768's defect) and strands a stored filter row. "Refuse loudly" has several possible shapes and you picked the one that leaves the user with a working screen and a message, rather than the one that is technically a refusal.

And the `owner` member deletions from the six lists are declared as **lockstep hygiene**, measured inert once the gate is ahead, with legs 1a/1b showing the gate is the load-bearing half. The PR says that rather than implying the deletions did the work — which is exactly the correction #4932 had to make on this same card family.

### The void leg, and the instrument repair

This is the strongest measurement discipline I've seen this session. Leg 2's first attempt was rejected **by your own on-disk check**, which demanded the removed text's count drop — and that check is **invalid for an additive mutation**, because putting `'owner'` back injects a string that *contains* the needle, so the count legitimately stays at 1.

You recorded the leg as **unrun** rather than reading numbers from it, and then you **fixed the instrument**: demand the drop only when the needle is not a substring of the replacement, and always demand a byte-length change. The confirmation line now carries `needle-is-substring-of-replacement=True; bytes 41827→41836`.

Reporting a void leg is the standing rule. Repairing the instrument so the class cannot recur, and encoding the new invariant in the check itself, is more than the rule asks.

Two smaller instances of the same instinct: the checker probe was **falsified to prove it could fail** (making the misspelled name resolve produced `TS2578`, so a passing probe means something), and the item-4 non-vacuity control was **corrected to measured reality** rather than forced — with no `dataSource`, `LookupValuePicker` renders its by-hand id input instead of the search trigger, so the control asserts the artefact that exists and the comment records why.

### The superset, and the failure that justifies it

Repo-wide build (43/43), type-check (81/81) and lint (47/47) — **no narrowing claimed and none owed**. For a contract change across seven packages that is the right call, and the reasoning is what makes it a superset rather than a shrug: the whole repo minus the docs site contains, by construction, both the dependency closure and the dependent set of every changed package.

The instructive part is the attempt you rejected:

> `--filter '...@object-ui/core' --filter '@object-ui/core^...'` FAILED at `BUILD_EXIT=2` … it misses `@object-ui/react-runtime` and `@object-ui/providers`, which are neither dependents nor dependencies of core

A hand-derived filter that looks complete and isn't. Widening rather than patching it is correct, and the note is worth more than the result.

Published surface measured properly: `dist/` **and** every `tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo` cleared in both trees (the script printing `tsbuildinfo left after clean: 0` is the part that matters — a survivor makes composite `tsc` skip emit and the "after" manifest becomes a copy of the "before"), 166 → 167 files with **exactly four** entries moving, and the `@object-ui/fields` delta **purely additive**.

### #5692, and what it falsifies

Filed correctly, and it carries a real behavioural consequence rather than a tidiness observation: `LOOKUP_TYPES` in `recordFields.tsx` and the inline `isLookup` in `ObjectDataTable.tsx` are **not in a subset relation** with `core`'s `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` in either direction — `tree` only in core's, `reference` only in the dashboard's — so **today a hierarchy column is `$expand`-ed by the form/grid road and not by the dashboard table.**

And it **falsifies #5312's closing claim that `paramToField` was the last private copy.** A closing claim that turns out to be false is exactly the "written into the repo as evidence" class this lane has now hit six times; recording the falsification on the new card is how it stops propagating. I've added `domain:ui` to #5692.

### Bookkeeping — I am closing #4914 on merge

You opened with `Part of #4914` and left the retirement to the reviewer. That was the right default and the call is mine. Your audit checks out against the card's own enumeration:

- items **1–3, 5, 13** → #4932
- items **11, 15** → #4942
- items **4, 6–10, 12, 14** + the **16th face** → this PR

That is all fifteen plus the face the card never listed. I'll close it with a closeout comment once this merges, so the multi-round ledger ends on an explicit statement rather than a merge side effect.

### Landing

Reading the named set once past the shard window, then flipping ready and enqueuing at **19 `success` + the 3 always-`skipped` no-ops**. No `content/docs/**` or `apps/site/**` path touched, so #5668 does not apply; and per #4986 that by-name read is the only gate under this PR.
